courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Elementary Latin I
courses.description: Grammar and reading for students who have had no work in Latin.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Elementary Latin II
courses.description: Grammar and reading of easy prose.
courses.prereqText: LAT 101 or one year of high school Latin.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Intermediate Latin
courses.description: Review of grammar; reading of easy narrative prose.
courses.prereqText: LAT 102 or two years of high school Latin.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Intro to Latin Literature
courses.description: Continuation of LAT 201, with readings chiefly in Latin poetic literature.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Survey of Latin Literature
courses.description: Advanced level readings in classical Latin literature. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated for a total of 6 undergraduate hours or 8 graduate hours in separate semesters, if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: LAT 202 or four years of high school Latin.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Intermediate Prose Composition
courses.description: Practice in the writing of Latin prose. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Medieval Latin
courses.description: Literary and historical texts in prose and poetry will be read in the original; the course will also cover patristic writings. Same as MDVL 460. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Two years of college Latin or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Readings in Latin Literature
courses.description: Readings in authors or special topics chosen by the instructor from the entire extant literature in Latin. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated in separate terms, if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: Three years of college Latin or equivalent, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Senior Thesis
courses.description: Thesis and honors. For candidates for honors in Latin and for other seniors. 2 or 4 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.
courses.prereqText: Senior standing and consent of Classics Honors Program.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Independent Reading
courses.description: See Department of the Classics for information. 1 to 4 undergraduate hours. 1 to 4 graduate hours. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 8 undergraduate hours or 12 graduate hours.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Advanced Prose Composition
courses.description: Practice in writing Latin prose, with special attention to stylistic questions.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Proseminar
courses.description: Alternating poetry and prose, concentrates on a major author from one of the following areas: epic, oratory, lyric and elegiac poetry, history, drama, philosophy, satire, or epistolography. Areas normally follow this sequence in successive years. May be repeated to a maximum of 20 hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Special Disciplines
courses.description: Variable content course concentrating on an area such as comparative grammar, epigraphy, metrics, palaeography, or papyrology. May be repeated if topics vary.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Latin Seminar
courses.description: Research on special problems of Latin literature; required of all majors in classical philology. May be repeated if topics vary.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Intro to Classical Studies
courses.description: Introductory survey for graduate students in classics; prepares students for work at the graduate level and surveys basic bibliography and methodology.

courses.subject: LAT
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Guidance in writing theses for advanced degrees. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in the same term or in separate terms.
